purpose: Hand decisions that override the automatic status in QUANTITY_LEXICON.tsv. Each entry says why. A status here is still subject to owner or Latinist review; it is not a Latinist's verdict.

entries.note: Long ā before a vowel is an exception to A&G §603.a. L&S writes Gāĭus and notes it is trisyllabic in Catullus 10.30; some teaching texts say Gāj-jus. Syllables and stress follow L&S here. Listen for two versus three syllables (LATIN_UNRESOLVED.md U-05)
Post-classical word (LX-028). A vowel before ns is long (A&G §603.d), so the con- should be printed recōnstrūctiō. Owner decision: correct the macron or drop the Latin word

Hidden quantity before gn. A&G §603.d says a vowel before gn is long (māgnus); the course prints magnus, as many modern texts do. Stress is unaffected because the syllable is heavy either way. Owner choice of convention
First i stands before gn: long by A&G §603.d (sīgnificātiō), printed short. Same convention choice as magnus. Other vowels agree with L&S
L&S marks the second vowel as common (tŏnī̆trus). Printed short, the stress is TO-ni-trus; long, it would be to-NĪ-trus. Check the recording against the printed form
Pronoun hic with short i (the adverb hīc is a different word, also in the course). The automatic check matched the adverb. Checked in the Latin audit (LX-029)
vĭr, vĭri in L&S. Collatinus matched vīrus (poison)
Short i before a vowel (A&G §603.a). The automatic check compared the nominative trēs/trīs
Infinitive stāre with long ā (1st conjugation, A&G §184). The supine stătum has a short a and does not apply
Present audit with short final i (A&G §167). Collatinus compared the supine stem audīt-
Hidden long ā. L&S records the inscriptional spelling MAARCVS, where the doubled vowel marks length
Hidden long vowel in lēctus, rēctus (from legō, regō), following the usual modern marking (Lachmann's law). L&S does not mark these vowels. Stress is unaffected
entries.source: A&G §603 (quantity of stem syllables learned from usage)

entries.note: Long vowel before ns, as printed
Short i in -ibus (3rd declension). Stress FON-ti-bus. The o is short in the oblique stem font-; only the nominative fōns has the long vowel before ns
3rd-conjugation infinitive in short -ere, so the stress is on the first syllable. Collatinus also offers ēmereō and ēdō, which do not apply
A vowel before a vowel is normally short (A&G §603.a), so dĕest; many teaching texts print dēest. Convention choice (LATIN_UNRESOLVED.md U-03)
Stem vowels agree with L&S. The long penult is the regular ending: imperfect -ēbat (A&G §168.b) and 2nd-conjugation infinitive -ēre (A&G §185)
